correctness.rationale: In any cyclic cover, every constant palindrome requires two loop-edge appearances and each pair of opposite nonconstant palindromes requires two distinct adjacent equal-pair labels, hence at least three traversals of its unordered edge. For even alphabets the baseline edge multigraph has odd degrees at every vertex and forces at least q/2 extra off-diagonal edges. A connected complete looped graph, augmented by a perfect matching for even q, has an Euler circuit. Expanding every first nonloop traversal a-b to a-b-a-b and every loop to a-a-a realizes all palindromes at the lower bound. Saturation proves that excess edges form a perfect matching. A real standalone verifier constructs and checks q=2..30 and independently brute-force searches q<=4; those finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General SCS approximation algorithms and universal-cycle Euler conditions apply algorithmically to finite inputs but supply neither the explicit all-q minimum nor the equality structure. Strict universal cycles require exactly-once windows without extraneous factors, unlike the present problem. Orientable sequences forbid reverse-duplicate windows, the opposite orientation constraint. A general polynomial algorithm would not by itself imply this closed-form identity without its specializing calculation.

originality.rationale: The all-alphabet shortest-length identity and equality-case perfect-matching rigidity were compared with the full text of Chen--Kitaev--Sun (2019/2020), the relevant general shortest-superstring and orientable-sequence formulations, published research-record semantic searches, and related mathematical results previously inspected. The universal-cycle literature imposes exact factor occurrence and no filler, while this problem is at-least-once cyclic coverage with unrestricted fillers. No equivalent quantitative implication or stronger result was found in the inspected material. Historical graph-walk literature may contain an implicit specialization; independent search remains a residual risk, not a proof of absolute novelty.
residual_risks: An earlier minimum Eulerian superwalk or special palindrome-superstring calculation could imply the closed form under an unrecognized alias.
The approximation-oriented shortest-superstring and orientable-sequence papers were compared at abstract/summary level only, not full-text theorem-by-theorem.
No exhaustive bibliographic or historical novelty certification; external independent validation not performed.

value.rationale: The shortest cyclic coverage length for a natural reversal-fixed test language is a complete all-alphabet optimization invariant, with exact q/2 parity overhead for even alphabets and a necessary-and-realizable classification of optimal adjacency profiles. These identify the unique type of obstruction and yield an explicit construction for all alphabets, beyond a routine finite census. The exact alphabet-parity effect matters for minimal cyclic test patterns and restricted universal covering words.
